about: Free Palestine, Inc.? A visual essay testing a thesis — that pro-Palestine activism outside Gaza has become an economy of merchandise, fundraising and attention that does not need the war to end — against the record: Gaza's own numbers, the hashtags, the merchandise, the money, the protests, and the claims in circulation, each checked.

search.text: Google searches for 'Free Palestine' in the US were almost nil until 9 October 2023, then spiked; interest correlated with the 2020 Democratic vote share by state.

attention.gap: Neither Instagram nor Google publishes hashtag or phrase counts by country that this page could read. Country-by-country figures for India and the US are therefore not shown rather than estimated.

offCampus.text: About 7 in 10 pro-Palestine events the Crowd Counting Consortium logged were away from campuses.

abroad.what: Protesters climbed the Royal Artillery Memorial at Hyde Park Corner after a march; police said no law was broken. The government then made climbing war memorials an offence.
A philosophy student tried to set fire to a crowded kosher pizzeria; investigators linked him to extremist antisemitic ideology. The reports found do not tie it to a protest.
The Bombay High Court refused the CPI(M) a Gaza rally — 'be patriots', 'look at your own country'. Police later allowed a peaceful assembly at Azad Maidan.
During a national Gaza strike, a group tried to force into Centrale station; about 60 police were injured and around ten people arrested.

election.text: Hamas won the last Palestinian legislative election, in January 2006: 74 of 132 seats, with 44.45% of the vote to Fatah's 41.43%.

claims.claim: 70,000 Gazans are dead.
claims.finding: 74,389 by 13 October 2026, by the Gaza health ministry's count.

claims.claim: Hamas killed roughly 1,200 Israelis.
claims.finding: About 1,200 killed on 7 October 2023.

claims.claim: Amazon keffiyeh sales surged 75% in 56 days.
claims.finding: Unit sales, 7 October–2 December 2023 against the previous 56 days, per Jungle Scout via Reuters.

claims.claim: The last West Bank workshop watched its output vanish in days.
claims.finding: Its US stock sold out in two days — because demand rose 50–70%. The boom went to the Palestinian factory.

claims.claim: Fast-fashion fakes flooded the market.
claims.finding: No figures found.

claims.claim: 1,360+ US student demonstrations, 170+ encampments, 3,100+ arrests.
claims.finding: The Crowd Counting Consortium logged thousands of campus protest days, 130+ encampments and 3,600+ arrests; 3,100+ is Wikipedia's count.

claims.claim: Campuses became theatres of chaos.
claims.finding: Of 12,400 US pro-Palestine protests in eight months, 167 had property damage and 18 police injuries reported — about 1.3% and 0.1%.

claims.claim: London protesters climbed the Battle of Britain memorial; one made a Nazi salute.
claims.finding: It was the Royal Artillery Memorial, in November 2023. No report of a Nazi salute was found.

claims.claim: A Milan march turned into looting and arson near the Duomo.
claims.finding: Clashes at Centrale station on 22 September 2025 left about 60 police injured; no looting or arson near the Duomo was reported.

claims.claim: A Madrid philosophy student tried to burn a pizzeria in reprisal for Gaza.
claims.finding: He tried to burn a crowded kosher pizzeria in March 2025; investigators called it antisemitic. The reports found give no Gaza motive.

claims.claim: In the French riots, Palestinian flags appeared among looters.
claims.finding: Not found in the reporting checked.

claims.claim: About 20 US pro-Palestinian groups raised $250 million in five years.
claims.finding: Israel's Diaspora Affairs ministry's figure for 2020–2025; not independently verified.

claims.claim: UNRWA USA collected over $51 million in 2024.
claims.finding: Its director expected over $51 million; it raised $32 million in 2023 and about $4 million a year before the war. No filed 2024 figure found.

claims.claim: SJP chapters draw multi-million-dollar flows; celebrities give millions.
claims.finding: No figures found.

claims.claim: Gaza's population fell 10.6% to about 2.13 million.
claims.finding: PCBS, end of 2025, against the pre-war estimate.

claims.claim: GDP fell 83% in 2024; per-capita output $161–212; unemployment 78%.
claims.finding: UNCTAD: $161 in 2024, $212 in 2025; 78% unemployment.

claims.claim: Reconstruction needs are $70–71.5 billion.
claims.finding: UN, EU and World Bank assessment; UNCTAD's later figure $71.5 billion.

claims.claim: Hamas documents show 15–25% of aid diverted.
claims.finding: From documents Israel seized, as reported by the WSJ and the IDF; not independently audited.

claims.claim: UNRWA employees took part in 7 October.
claims.finding: The UN's oversight office found 9 of 19 investigated may have been involved; all were dismissed.

claims.claim: Hamas won the last elections held in Gaza.
claims.finding: January 2006: 74 of 132 seats.

claims.claim: The money comes from a 'Jewish-controlled' industry.
claims.finding: An antisemitic trope, not a factual claim. Left out of this page.

tests.test: Does the merchandise money reach Gaza?
tests.for: Most sellers publish no audit of what share of revenue reaches Gaza.
tests.against: The West Bank's own factory saw sales rise 50–70%; some sellers pledge all profits to named charities.

tests.test: Does the fundraising grow with the war?
tests.for: UNRWA USA went from about $4 million a year to $32 million in 2023 and an expected $51 million in 2024.
tests.against: That is a refugee-aid charity's income rising with need; $51 million is 0.07% of Gaza's $71.5 billion reconstruction bill.

tests.test: Is the protest movement a performance of disorder?
tests.for: Milan's station clashes; the memorial climb; arrests in the thousands.
tests.against: About 98.7% of 12,400 US protests had no property damage reported; 7 in 10 were off campus.

tests.test: Does the movement need the war to continue?
tests.for: Attention, sales and donations all rose after 7 October.
tests.against: Attention spiked and decayed with events; no data shows organisers working against a ceasefire.
